name: The MindGames Challenge: Theory-of-Mind and Game Intelligence in LLM Agents (NeurIPS 2025 Competition)
authors_org: Organizers: Kevin Wang, Jianzhu Yao, Yihan Jiang, Benjamin Finch, Viraj Nadkarni, Benjamin Kempinski, Anna C. M. Thoeni, Mathieu Lauriere, Maria Polukarov, Pramod Viswanath, Tal Kachman, Yoram Bachrach, Zhangyang 'Atlas' Wang (affiliations include UT Austin / VITA Group, Radboud University, Princeton, and others).
games_supported: Four games spanning a spectrum of social/strategic reasoning: Werewolf (adversarial social deduction), Stag Hunt (mixed-motive cooperation), Colonel Blotto (resource-contested competition), and Hanabi (communication-constrained cooperation). Werewolf is the core social-deduction game.
num_players: Varies by game: Werewolf is a multi-player social-deduction game; Hanabi is typically 2-5 players; Stag Hunt is a 2-player coordination game; Colonel Blotto is a 2-player resource-allocation game. [uncertain]
hidden_role_mechanic: Hidden roles appear chiefly in the Werewolf track, where a minority of werewolves are secretly assigned among villagers and special roles, and players must infer identities from discussion. The other three games involve hidden intentions/strategies rather than hidden roles.
rule_variant_coverage: Four distinct games are supported, and the Werewolf component has multiple tracks (e.g., Efficient, Unlimited, and a Generalization track), giving breadth across both game types and Werewolf rule/budget variants. [uncertain]
multimodal_support: No. Agents communicate via natural language only; no video, audio, or voice-prosody modalities.
reasoning_paradigm: Open-ended: participants build agents (typically LLM-powered) that must communicate via natural language, reason about hidden states and competing objectives, and dynamically adapt strategies over repeated interactions. The paradigm (ReAct, CoT, search, RL) is left to each entrant. [uncertain]
memory_mechanism: Determined by each submitted agent; the competition does not mandate a memory mechanism. Agents must track game history across multi-turn and repeated interactions, with implementation left to participants. [uncertain]
belief_state_representation: Determined by each submitted agent. The competition is explicitly about theory of mind, so agents are expected to model and update beliefs about other agents' hidden states, but the representation (probabilistic, natural-language, latent) is entrant-defined. [uncertain]
planning_approach: Entrant-defined. Agents must plan in longer-horizon dynamic environments and adapt strategies in repeated/iterative interactions; the competition does not prescribe a planning method. [uncertain]
action_tool_design: The arena exposes per-game action and communication interfaces (natural-language messages, votes, and game-specific moves) that submitted agents respond to; agents are wrapped to a standard arena API. [uncertain]
theory_of_mind_evaluation: Theory of mind is the central evaluation target: the challenge explicitly tests modeling others' beliefs, detecting deception, coordinating under uncertainty, and long-horizon planning. ToM is measured indirectly through head-to-head performance across the four games rather than via a dedicated belief-accuracy probe.
turn_structure: Game-specific turn structures (e.g., Werewolf day/night discussion and voting rounds; Hanabi sequential card plays; Stag Hunt and Blotto simultaneous decisions). Agents act over repeated and iterative interactions. [uncertain]
phase_handling: Each game manages its own phases via the arena engine (e.g., Werewolf night/day/discussion/voting phases); the platform orchestrates phase transitions per game. [uncertain]
communication_protocol: Natural-language communication is required; channels are game-specific (public discussion and votes in Werewolf, constrained hint signals in Hanabi, action choices in Stag Hunt and Blotto). [uncertain]
communication_synchrony: Game-dependent: turn-based discussion in Werewolf and Hanabi; simultaneous decision-making in Stag Hunt and Colonel Blotto. The arena schedules turns per game. [uncertain]
metrics: Performance is measured by head-to-head competition results aggregated into TrueSkill ratings across the four games; per-game win/score outcomes feed the rating.
deception_metric_design: No dedicated deception metric. Deception (especially in Werewolf) is captured implicitly through head-to-head win/loss outcomes and the resulting TrueSkill rating rather than a lie taxonomy or detector surrogate. [uncertain]
persuasion_modeling: Not explicitly modeled as a separate metric; persuasive ability in Werewolf discussion is reflected only indirectly in match outcomes and ratings. [uncertain]
rating_system: TrueSkill. Agents are rated via TrueSkill computed from head-to-head matches in a live arena.
competition_format: A live, head-to-head tournament arena across the four games, with two/three divisions (Open and Efficient agent divisions; Werewolf has Efficient, Unlimited, and Generalization tracks). Cross-play between submitted agents, July-October 2025, $10K prize pool, results presented at NeurIPS 2025 (December 7, 2025).
llms_evaluated: Open: participants choose their own LLM backends (any model, including large proprietary or open models); the Efficient division constrains model size/compute. Specific top entrants' models are not enumerated here. [uncertain]
human_baseline_comparison: No formal human baseline; the arena ranks submitted agents against each other via TrueSkill rather than against human players. [uncertain]
data_source_provenance: Synthetic agent-vs-agent gameplay generated live in the competition arena; no curated human gameplay data.
training_paradigm: Entrant-defined. Participants may use tuning-free prompting, fine-tuning, or RL; the competition does not prescribe a training paradigm and the Efficient division constrains resources. [uncertain]
agent_controllability: Not a controllability study; agents are submissions whose strength is whatever entrants achieve. Difficulty is fixed by the games and the opponent pool. [uncertain]
strategy_space_analysis: The competition emphasizes generalization across diverse strategic settings (including a Werewolf Generalization track), implicitly probing strategy breadth, but a formal strategy-space analysis is up to organizers' post-hoc reports. [uncertain]
prompt_optimizer_used: Entrant-defined; not mandated by the competition. Some teams may use DSPy/prompt optimizers, but this is not prescribed. [uncertain]
rl_algorithm: Entrant-defined; not mandated. Teams may apply RL/preference optimization to their agents. [uncertain]
reward_design: The competition's evaluation signal is win/loss outcomes across the four games aggregated via TrueSkill; any internal training reward is entrant-defined. [uncertain]
optimization_target: Entrant-defined (prompts, demonstrations, or policy weights); the competition targets maximizing TrueSkill across the four games. [uncertain]
self_play_loop: Self-play may be used by participants to train their agents; the arena itself runs cross-play among submissions rather than a shared training self-play loop. [uncertain]
credit_assignment: Not specified by the competition; any multi-turn credit assignment is internal to each submitted agent. [uncertain]
optimization_cost: Constrained in the Efficient division (limited compute/model size); the Open division allows higher compute. Exact budgets are not specified here. [uncertain]
framework_used: A custom live competition arena platform (MindGames Arena) hosting the four games with a standardized agent API. [uncertain]
open_source: Partially. The arena and starter kits are made available to participants via mindgamesarena.com; full open-source status of the platform is not fully confirmed. [uncertain]
reproducibility: Moderate. The competition provides a shared arena, game environments, and starter code, but final results depend on submitted agents and proprietary models, and the live-arena format limits exact re-runs. [uncertain]
key_results: As a competition (concluded December 2025), headline outcomes are the TrueSkill leaderboards across Werewolf, Stag Hunt, Colonel Blotto, and Hanabi and the identification of top agents in the Open and Efficient divisions. The challenge demonstrates that theory-of-mind capacities (belief modeling, deception detection, coordination under uncertainty, long-horizon planning) remain a key differentiator among LLM agents. Detailed final rankings are not enumerated here. [uncertain]
identified_limitations: Theory-of-mind capabilities of current LLM agents remain limited, motivating the competition. As a live arena, results are tied to the submission pool and proprietary models, limiting standardized comparison and exact reproducibility. [uncertain]
deception_emergence: The Werewolf track inherently elicits deceptive play (werewolves lying to evade detection); emergent deception is observed through gameplay, but the competition reports outcomes via TrueSkill rather than a formal deception-emergence analysis. [uncertain]
deceiver_detector_asymmetry: Not formally measured. The competition does not isolate deceiver-vs-detector capability; any asymmetry is implicit in Werewolf match outcomes. [uncertain]
